title: feat(core,app-shell,plugin-view,i18n): the delete confirmation names the record and confirms with a destructive Delete (objectui#11695)
body:
Fixes #11695

Clause-②: yes

Session: `https://claude.ai/code/session_01CGZy1BGCjdN5cXqL9cnvB8` (os-dev seat `domain:ui#3`, PM loop round 1).

## What changes

A record delete confirmation now names what it deletes and confirms with a destructive "Delete" button:

- **One record:** the title names the object label and the record's display name. en: `Delete Product "QA Widget 0"?`. zh: `删除Product“QA Widget 0”？`.
- **A selection:** the title counts it: `Delete 3 Product records?` (zh `删除 3 条 Product 记录？`).
- **Confirm button:** it reads "Delete" (zh 删除) and is painted with `buttonVariants({ variant: 'destructive' })`.
- **Body:** unchanged. It is the plain delete question, the batch question, or ADR-0094's reset question for a package-owned permission set.

Every delete dialog takes this copy from one builder, `recordDelete.confirmCopy(deps, target)` in `@object-ui/core`. It sits beside the existing `confirmText`, which is now its one-record body. The name comes from `getRecordDisplayName`, the ADR-0079 resolver the record page already uses for its title. Each host passes its object definition, so a declared `nameField` wins.

| Surface | Producer | What it does now |
|---|---|---|
| Console object list, row Delete and bulk Delete (the card's repro) | `@object-ui/app-shell` `useObjectActions`, called by app-shell `ObjectView` | `deleteRecord` and the new `deleteRecords` ask `onConfirm` with the copy and `destructive: true`, then run the delete through the runner with no `confirmText` |
| Record page Delete | `@object-ui/app-shell` `RecordDetailView`, the `sys_delete` header action | Same copy, read from the readable row (a denied name field reads as absent). A package-owned permission set now gets the reset question here too |
| Registered `object-view` grid Delete | `@object-ui/plugin-view` `ObjectView`, `deleteConfirmDialog` | Same copy, with the confirm button painted destructive |
| The console's confirm dialog | `@object-ui/app-shell` `ActionConfirmDialog` | Paints its confirm button destructive when `options.destructive` is set. Its options type is now the published `ConfirmationHandler` options, not a copy |

The `ConfirmationHandler` options in `@object-ui/core` gain `destructive?: boolean`. Every other confirmation keeps "Confirm Action" / "Continue" in the primary style. The `actionConfirm.*` text is unchanged.

`packages/components/src/ui/alert-dialog.tsx` is not touched (No-Touch zone, AGENTS.md #7). The destructive style is a className override at each call site. objectui#8978's `actionVariant` uses the same approach in the `alert-dialog` renderer.

## Premise check on origin/main `0cfe772`, hypothesis by hypothesis

1. plugin-view's `deleteConfirmDialog` used `actionConfirm.title` / `actionConfirm.confirm`, with `recordDelete.confirmText` as the body. **Held.**
2. `actionConfirm.title` / `.confirm` are shared. **Held.** `ActionConfirmDialog` falls back to them for every action-runner confirmation. Their text is unchanged; the delete has its own keys.
3. **The detail page's producer** is `RecordDetailView` in `packages/app-shell`, not `packages/plugin-detail`. Its `sys_delete` action asked `detail.deleteConfirmation` through the page's confirm handler with one argument.
   - **The card's repro path (console list, row menu, Delete) never reaches plugin-view.** The console list's `onDelete` calls `useObjectActions.deleteRecord`, which handed the action runner a `confirmText`.
   - The runner calls the confirm handler with one argument. So the console dialog could only ever show its generic title and "Continue".
   - Both producers are changed here. The record page falls under the claim's "the dev locates it" clause. The console list's producer adds three app-shell files: `useObjectActions.ts`, `ActionConfirmDialog.tsx` and `ObjectView.tsx`.
4. The title resolver exists: `getRecordDisplayName` (`@object-ui/core`). **Reused**, no new resolver.
5. objectui#11728 (`objectPluralLabel`) was still open when this was built (REST read before implementation: `merged: false`). So the batch title uses the singular label with a count family that mirrors `objectActions.bulkDeleteSuccess` (`Delete 3 Product records?`). That is the same shape as the toast that follows. It has merged since (main `6be0f7a`). The Acceptance notes explain why this PR still keeps the count-agreeing noun.

objectui#8978: the card body says it "added the destructive confirm button to `alert-dialog`", and the triage says there is "no destructive variant". Both are partly right:
- It added `actionVariant` to the `alert-dialog` **renderer** (`packages/components/src/renderers/overlay/alert-dialog.tsx`), as a className override.
- The `ui/alert-dialog.tsx` **primitive** still bakes in `buttonVariants()` with no variant.

## Keys

- **New in all ten packs**, under `objectActions`:
  - `deleteConfirmTitle` (`{{label}}`, `{{name}}`);
  - the `bulkDeleteConfirmTitle` count family (`{{count}}`, `{{label}}`). Each pack's slots mirror its own `bulkDeleteSuccess` family: es/fr/pt `_many`, ru `_few`/`_many`, ar all six;
  - `deleteConfirmButton`.
- **Unchanged:** no existing value changed and no key was removed.
- **plugin-view:** its English map for hosts without a translation provider gains the new rows. It drops `actionConfirm.title` / `.confirm`, which that host no longer asks for.
- **de quote census:** `de-quote-pairing-3876.test.ts` moves from 70 to 71 for the title's one matched „…“ pair.

The console list now passes its translated object label to `useObjectActions` (`objectLabel(objectDef)`, the label its header shows), so the delete toasts use that label too. With no translation bundle it is `objectDef.label`, as before.

**Console compile: narrowed, not run.**
- `apps/console` resolves `@object-ui/*` through built `dist`; its tsconfig has no `paths`.
- Its source names none of the changed symbols. A search for `useObjectActions|ActionConfirmDialog|ConfirmDialogState|ConfirmationHandler|recordDelete` in `apps/console/src` finds one hit, in a comment.
- The control search for `from '@object-ui/app-shell'` does find the console's real imports.
- So the console reads only app-shell's emitted declarations, and that source passes the type-check above.

## Reverse verification (ablation)

Every leg ran through objectstack's `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, which checks three things:
- the anchor must hit;
- the file's blob must change;
- the restore is proven by the blob matching HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

The expected direction for every leg was red.

| Leg | Mutation (anchor hit once, blob changed) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1, destructive paint | `ActionConfirmDialog`: the `options.destructive` className replaced by `className={undefined}` | 6 failed, 4 passed. Red: the console list's row and batch in en and zh, and the record page in en and zh, all on `bg-destructive`. The primary-style controls stayed green |
| 2, delete label | `recordDelete.confirmCopy`: `deleteConfirmButton` replaced by `actionConfirm.confirm` | 16 failed, 22 passed, across core (copy mismatch), the console list, the record page and plugin-view (no "Delete" button found) |
| 3, name field | `useObjectActions.deleteRecord`: `objectDef` dropped from the copy's deps | 2 failed, 4 passed. The row title read `Delete Product "SKU-1"?` (a record key) instead of the declared `nameField` value |
| type-level | `RecordDetailView`: `destructive: true` misspelled `destructiv` | `tsc --noEmit` reports TS2561 on that key against the rebuilt `ConfirmationHandler` options |

## Acceptance notes

- **Plural label.** objectui#11728 landed after this was built, but the batch title deliberately keeps "N {{label}} records" rather than "N {{pluralLabel}}".
  - With "records", count agreement lives in a pack noun that each language inflects (ru записи/записей, ar six forms).
  - A metadata plural label has one form per object, so it cannot agree with a count.
  - It is the same pattern as the toast that follows.
  - Changing to "Delete 3 Products?" would only change pack values, not code.
- **Bulk body.** The batch dialog's body is still `console.objectView.bulkDeleteConfirm` ("Delete N selected records? This cannot be undone."), so the title and the body both ask. The claim limited locale edits to new delete keys, so no existing value was changed.
- **Ask before `execute`.** `useObjectActions` now asks before `execute`, so the hook's `loading` is false while the dialog is open. No code in the repo reads that hook's `loading` or `error`. A cancel still returns the runner's former `{ success: false, error: 'Action cancelled by user' }`.
- **Nameless rows.** A row with no resolvable name shows the resolver's English `Record #id` fallback, the same one every other surface shows.
- **Same class, not touched.** Recorded only, no card filed, carrier: none:
  - `plugin-detail` `DetailView` still deletes through the native `window.confirm`, with the authorable `deleteConfirmation` or the generic `detail.deleteConfirmation`. That is the drawer and panel detail used by gantt rows and similar.
  - app-shell's "delete saved view" confirm says "Delete" but uses the primary style.
  - After a package-owned permission set is reset, the record page's delete still toasts "Record deleted". The list's shared `recordDelete.run` toasts the reset. Not measured through a public entry point.
- **plugin-view's label** is still the raw `objectSchema.label`, the one its form titles and toasts already use.
- **Merge with current main** (`ded4494`) is textually clean (`git merge-tree`). main's de pack quote count is unchanged since the base, so the census pin does not collide.
